objective: Produce the complete list of external readers of config.json (bounded probe) and deliver a route-independent YAML config store (same interface as JsonConfigStore, parity-tested), so the next stage can implement either route (A: YAML primary + JSON export mirror, B: full YAML cutover) without re-planning the foundation.
in_scope: bounded probe: inventory every external reader of config.json (repo grep, CI config, deploy scripts, deploy runbook) with a recorded route recommendation
YamlConfigStore implementing the frozen store interface (get/set/save/as_dict, REQUIRED_KEYS, ConfigError on missing file) over a vendored YAML-subset parser (flat dict of scalars, stdlib-only)
parity test suite proving YamlConfigStore behaves exactly like JsonConfigStore on the existing test matrix

out_of_scope.item: Route A implementation: JSON export mirror regenerated on save + keeping uncontrolled readers working
out_of_scope.reason: route depends on probe evidence (the reader list) that does not exist yet

out_of_scope.item: Route B implementation: full YAML cutover, updating owned readers, deleting config.json
out_of_scope.reason: route depends on probe evidence (the reader list) that does not exist yet

out_of_scope.item: wiring loader.py / cli.py to the YAML store
out_of_scope.reason: wiring is route-specific (Route A keeps JSON readers alive; Route B updates them); decided by the next stage
the probe must first establish the complete set of external readers; check.sh handling is route-specific

out_of_scope.item: config schema changes (new keys, nested structures, new validation rules)
out_of_scope.reason: not requested; the data shape is frozen (C2)

out_of_scope.item: migration tooling for existing config.json files
out_of_scope.reason: migration strategy follows the route decision; planned in the next stage

frozen_assumptions.statement: the config data shape is a flat dict of scalar values (str/number/bool)
frozen_assumptions.rationale: all current usages (JsonConfigStore get/set, cli set, deploy/check.sh key grep) deal in flat scalar keys; invalidation: the probe or store work encounters nested structures — the YAML-subset scope must then be widened

frozen_assumptions.statement: the platform constraint is stdlib-only, so YAML parsing must be a small vendored subset parser, not a third-party dependency
frozen_assumptions.rationale: README Platform notes; invalidation: subset proves infeasible for real configs — escalate a dependency request at the route stage, do not silently add one

frozen_architecture.decision: loader.py and cli.py stay on JsonConfigStore in this stage; YamlConfigStore is additive and unwired (existing behavior and tests untouched until the route is chosen)
frozen_architecture.rationale: keeps startup validation and CLI behavior byte-identical while the route is unknown; the swap is the next stage's job behind seam S1

shared_contracts.spec: ConfigStore interface: get(key, default=None) -> value; set(key, value) -> None (persists immediately); save() -> None (persists current state); as_dict() -> dict (shallow copy). Class attribute REQUIRED_KEYS = ('app_name', 'env', 'log_level'). Constructor takes a file path; missing file raises ConfigError('config file missing: <path>'). Both JsonConfigStore and YamlConfigStore satisfy this interface identically.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: only via contract change request; the route stage wires the loader/cli against this interface, so changing it invalidates that wiring

shared_contracts.spec: config data shape: flat dict; required keys app_name (str), env (str), log_level (one of debug|info|warning|error); all values scalar (str/number/bool). No nested structures.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: route stage may only add keys (additive), never change required-key semantics

integration_seams.description: store parity boundary: YamlConfigStore (new) must be a drop-in replacement for JsonConfigStore (reference) at the C1 interface; the integration task runs the shared parity matrix (mirroring tests/test_config.py) against both implementations

acceptance.description: YamlConfigStore passes the same test matrix as JsonConfigStore: get/set roundtrip, save persistence, as_dict shallow copy, missing file raises ConfigError, REQUIRED_KEYS present on both classes
acceptance.positive_case: set('feature_x', true) then reload from file: get('feature_x') is true; as_dict() contains all keys
acceptance.negative_case: YamlConfigStore on a nonexistent path raises ConfigError with 'config file missing:' prefix
acceptance.failure_behavior: any matrix mismatch is a test failure in tests/test_yaml_store.py

acceptance.description: YAML roundtrip fidelity: save then reload from file returns identical data for the C2 shape
acceptance.positive_case: store a valid C2 config in a temp file, reload from disk, as_dict() returns a dict equal to the original
acceptance.negative_case: a config file with a nested value is rejected: the parser raises ConfigError with the documented subset message (stated in the parser module docstring)
acceptance.failure_behavior: roundtrip inequality is a test failure

acceptance.description: existing suite stays green: the full test suite exits 0, proving loader/cli are still on JSON in this stage
acceptance.positive_case: python -m unittest discover tests exits 0 with all pre-existing tests passing
acceptance.negative_case: any pre-existing test failing means DA-1 was violated
acceptance.evidence: python -m unittest discover tests -v (full suite, including new tests)

acceptance.description: probe deliverable: the plan artifact file records the complete external-reader list of config.json with a route recommendation, naming at minimum deploy/check.sh
acceptance.positive_case: the artifact file contains each reader with location + evidence (grep hit / runbook reference) and a 'Recommendation: Route A' or 'Recommendation: Route B' line followed by reasoning
acceptance.negative_case: a reader list that omits deploy/check.sh or contains no recommendation fails the gate
acceptance.failure_behavior: the closure test fails on a missing or incomplete artifact; the stage is then not acceptance-complete and the normal planning trigger cannot fire
acceptance.evidence: spike deliverable file in the plan dir (e.g. spike-reader-inventory.md) referenced by the stage checkpoint

constraints.rule: stdlib only; the YAML subset parser is vendored code inside the store module — no third-party package
probe is bounded to 30-60 minutes of work (repo grep + CI config + deploy scripts + runbook read); it does not become a research project

loader.py and cli.py are NOT modified in this stage (DA-1); their current behavior — CLI flags (--path, show, set) with the 'set <key> = <value>' success message, and the loader's ConfigError message shapes (config file missing / missing required config key / invalid log_level) — is an unchanged behavioral baseline that the route stage re-freezes as its own contracts

open_questions.question: does any real config in use contain nested values (which would break the A-1 flat-shape assumption)?
open_questions.resolution: the probe (T01) checks the actual config.json in the repo plus the deploy runbook examples; if nested data is found, A-1 is falsified and the YAML-subset scope widens at the next planning trigger

detailed_stage.objective: reader-inventory evidence + route-independent YAML store, both certain under either route

stages.objective: Route A: YAML becomes primary store, config.json regenerated as an export mirror on every save so uncontrolled external readers keep working; loader/cli wired behind S1; deploy/check.sh left untouched
depends_on_evidence: reader inventory shows external readers beyond owned tooling

stages.objective: Route B: full YAML cutover — loader/cli wired to YamlConfigStore, owned readers (deploy/check.sh etc.) updated, config.json deleted; migration step for the live file
depends_on_evidence: reader inventory shows only owned, updatable readers

stage_boundary.because: the stage ends at new evidence that can change the route (the complete external-reader list from the probe) and at the route-independent foundation being built and parity-proven (YamlConfigStore); route-specific work (JSON mirror vs reader updates + deletion) cannot be designed before the reader list exists
expected_new_evidence: complete list of external readers of config.json (repo grep + CI config + deploy scripts + runbook) with a route recommendation
decisions_deferred_until_then: whether config.json is kept as a regenerated export
how and when loader/cli switch to the YAML store
migration step for the live config.json
